490.brief_boundary_fact: Return is triggered by request during the term, not by termination, expiration, rejection, or conclusion.

334.brief_boundary_fact: Return and destruction are triggered by the disclosing party's request only.

88.brief_boundary_fact: Return or destruction is required on request, without a termination trigger.

331.brief_boundary_fact: All furnished materials and copies must be returned after the business possibility is rejected or concluded.

238.brief_boundary_fact: The parties must return covered confidential information upon termination for any reason.

245.brief_boundary_fact: Return duties are expressly triggered by Project expiration or termination and by Agreement termination.

guidance.when: The source expressly makes return or destruction of protected information operative upon termination, expiration, rejection, or conclusion of the agreement, project, or contemplated relationship.
guidance.inspection: Separate the operative return or destruction duty from request-only duties, then verify that the stated trigger is an ending event and carry forward any scope limits or exceptions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the ending-event trigger together with the operative return or destruction language; include a governing list introduction when the duty is an item.

operations.rationale: Adds the missing generic distinction between an ending-event duty and a request-only return clause; absence of this sufficient condition does not imply NotMentioned.

490.brief_boundary_fact: The clause requires return and identifies no archival, legal, or other retained-copy exception.

334.brief_boundary_fact: Automatically created backup copies may remain in ordinary archival storage subject to access and confidentiality limits.

88.brief_boundary_fact: All originals and copy forms must be returned or destroyed, with no retention permission.

331.brief_boundary_fact: All copies accompany returned materials after the business possibility ends.

238.brief_boundary_fact: Documents and all copies must be returned or destroyed, without a retained-copy carve-out.

245.brief_boundary_fact: Backup information and one legal-department copy may expressly be retained under continuing restrictions.

guidance.when: The source expressly exempts identified copies or stored protected information from a return or deletion duty and permits their continued retention.
guidance.inspection: Read the general return or destruction rule with every overriding exception; identify what may remain, who or what system may hold it, its purpose, and continuing restrictions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention permission and any governing exception transition, plus material limits such as archival-only access, dispute purpose, or continuing confidentiality.

operations.rationale: Captures explicit post-return retention permissions while separating them from clauses that merely command return of all copies.

490.brief_boundary_fact: No clause prohibits revealing negotiations, agreement existence, receipt of information, or transaction terms.

334.brief_boundary_fact: The recipient may not reveal negotiations, receipt of evaluation material, or transaction terms and status without consent.

88.brief_boundary_fact: The existence of negotiations, discussions, consultations, or agreements in progress may not be released publicly absent written agreement.

331.brief_boundary_fact: The agreement regulates confidential information but does not impose secrecy on the fact of negotiations or agreement.

238.brief_boundary_fact: No separate transaction- or agreement-existence secrecy provision appears.

245.brief_boundary_fact: No clause separately protects the fact of negotiations or the agreement itself.

guidance.when: The source expressly prohibits disclosure of the existence or occurrence of negotiations, discussions, an agreement in progress, receipt of evaluation material, or terms or status of the contemplated transaction.
guidance.inspection: Distinguish secrecy of the deal process or agreement facts from ordinary secrecy of confidential information, and preserve consent, audience, and publicity qualifications.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the prohibition's governing language and each relied-on enumerated subject; a generic nondisclosure clause alone is insufficient.

operations.rationale: Corrects missed process-confidentiality language without broadening ordinary information confidentiality into secrecy of the agreement.

490.brief_boundary_fact: The source addresses copying through a prohibition conditioned on written permission and also requires return of copies.

334.brief_boundary_fact: It combines a consent-conditioned no-copy rule with automatic backup creation and archival retention.

88.brief_boundary_fact: The return clause expressly covers originals, copies, reproductions, and summaries but does not authorize creating them.

331.brief_boundary_fact: The return obligation covers all copies, without an express creation permission.

238.brief_boundary_fact: Ownership and return language covers documents and all copies, without authorizing their creation.

245.brief_boundary_fact: The source expressly permits necessary Project copies and identifies retained backup and legal copies.

guidance.when: A source clause expressly addresses making, reproducing, automatically creating, returning, destroying, or retaining copies of protected information.
guidance.inspection: Classify the copy language by legal function: affirmative exception, automatic-copy acknowledgement, consent-conditioned prohibition, mere reference to existing copies, return duty, or retention carve-out. Do not infer creation permission from employee access or generic safeguarding.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative copy wording and its governing condition or exception; read adjacent retention or return language when it changes the clause's function.

operations.rationale: Introduces a neutral polarity inspection because superficially similar copy references produced different labels and no single broad label implication safely covers them.

490.brief_boundary_fact: No express or implied license is granted under specified intellectual-property rights.

334.brief_boundary_fact: Neither the agreement nor disclosure grants a license or rights in evaluation material.

88.brief_boundary_fact: The information remains the discloser's property and no rights are granted except as otherwise provided.

331.brief_boundary_fact: Multiple clauses deny conveyed rights or licenses while preserving only a narrow review right.

238.brief_boundary_fact: Ownership remains with the discloser and express or implied license and product-use rights are denied.

245.brief_boundary_fact: Intellectual-property rights remain with the discloser and no right or license is granted.

guidance.when: The source expressly states that the agreement or disclosure grants, conveys, or confers no right or license in protected information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Identify the denied grant separately from ownership, limited-purpose use, and review permissions; preserve any express narrow exception without treating it as a general license.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative no-rights or no-license wording and any material exception; ownership language may be retained as independent support but is not a substitute for an express grant denial.

operations.rationale: Prevents a limited use permission from being mistaken for a contradiction of an express no-license or no-rights clause.
